Issued at 545 PM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

In the initial stages of the long term forecast period, our attention 
will remain focused on the broad upper level low over the Mid-
Mississippi River. While individual models continue to disagree upon 
this feature's evolution, it is generally progged to dig deeper into 
the Tennessee River Valley on Thanksgiving Day. Continuous height 
falls, cyclonic vorticity advection, and a seasonably moist airmass 
should all combine to yield widespread precipitation chances in 
Eastern Kentucky for the holiday. Precipitation should taper off on 
Black Friday as the system propagates off to the northeast, although 
its ejection speed and exact trajectory appear contingent upon 
how/if it phases with a shortwave moving up the east coast. Those 
details will play a role in determining what form of precipitation 
falls on the system's backside, but widespread hazardous weather 
appears unlikely in this particular setup. 

The majority of the precipitation that falls on Thanksgiving should 
come in the form of a plain, cool rain. The forecast area will be 
positioned firmly within the system's warm sector at the start of 
the period, with forecast model soundings keeping sub-850mb 
temperatures well above the freezing point through Thursday evening. 
Thick stratiform cloud cover should insulate the diurnal heating 
curve and keep surface temperatures stagnant in the 40s all day. The 
highest PoPs occur early on in the period, with the NBM resolving a 
95-100% chance of rain on Thursday morning. LREF probabilities for 
at least 0.5 inches of rain to fall before sunset are between 75 and 
95%. While such conditions are not conducive for outdoor holiday 
plans, the forecast area is poised to receive a highly-beneficial 
wetting rain on Thanksgiving. 

As we move into the winter holiday season later that evening/night, 
colder air is expected to wrap around the backside of the system. 
This could allow for some festive flakes to fly/fall, but 
accumulation potential appears limited by the marginal nature of 
this setup. If the center of the upper level low tracks directly 
overhead on Thanksgiving evening/night, there could be a window of 
time where enough ingredients are in place for snow to mix in with 
the rain. Critical thickness values are forecast to fall within the 
marginally-favorable 537-540 dam range in the immediate vicinity of 
the low's cold core center. Likewise, above-925mb temperatures are 
forecast to fall below freezing on the southern and western sides of 
the circulation. Given that surface low temperatures on Thanksgiving 
night will be relegated to the marginal 32-36 degree range by 
lingering cloud cover and subsequent radiational cooling insulation, 
the exact track of that low will prove crucial in determining p-
type. A more northerly trajectory would favor greater snow chances 
in the commonwealth, whereas a southerly trajectory could prevent 
the favorable ingredients from all overlapping. Any snow that falls 
would likely be on the wetter side of the snow ratio spectrum, but 
the antecedently warm grounds should limit accumulations outside of 
higher terrain locales. 10:1 snow ratio accumulation maps will 
not accurately capture this specific type of setup, and their 
output will likely bounce around in the coming days. This also
applies to probabilistic data that is rooted in standard snow
ratios. So, interests are encouraged to exercise caution as 
online buzz surrounding this event builds.  

Precipitation will linger into Black Friday before tapering off 
overnight into Saturday. Modeled height rises and warming 
temperatures on the backside of the system will likely facilitate a 
changeover back to a cold rain by mid-morning, and drier air should 
work its way back into the CWA on Saturday. The guidance suite 
resolves a brief period of shortwave ridging on Saturday morning. 
This should yield some degree of clearing and a noticeable warming 
trend for the first half of the weekend. However, diverging model 
solutions make it difficult to pinpoint specific sensible weather 
details beyond Saturday. The ECMWF and thus the NBM introduce the 
area's next chances for rain on Sunday, whereas the GFS camp of 
solutions keeps us in tamer quasi zonal flow through early next 
week. As models come to a consensus on the Thanksgiving low's path, 
there should be less forecast uncertainty cascading into the latter 
half of the forecast period. Therefore, interests with early week 
outdoor plans are encouraged to monitor for updates in the wake of 
the rather wet holiday.
